title: A lisse continuous sheaf has a lisse integral model on a nonempty reduced open
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $A=\mathcal O_E$ and $\varpi$ a uniformizer [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-pc-scheme]; noetherian means a finite affine cover by spectra of noetherian rings, and finite-dimensional means a finite bound on lengths of strict chains of irreducible closed subsets. Write $A_Y(V)=C(|V|,A)$ and $E_Y(V)=C(|V|,E)$ on the small pro-etale site of any locally closed subscheme $Y$ of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use sheaf modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and $S_Y(M)=E_Y\otimes_{A_Y}M$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Constructible integral means continuous-constructible as in [def-weil-pbc-continuous-constructible-module], with local models $A_Y\otimes_A P$ for finitely presented $A$-modules $P$ on finitely many locally closed strata. Assume that $X$ is nonempty and reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Let $L$ be an $E_X$-module sheaf pro-etale locally free of finite rank, meaning a pro-etale covering makes it a finite direct sum of its coefficient sheaf; ranks may vary and may be zero. There is a nonempty quasi-compact open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-open-immersion] and an $A_U$-module sheaf $M_U$ pro-etale locally free of finite rank such that $S_U(M_U)\cong j^{-1}L$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image].

source.place: Lemma 6.8.13, first paragraph, followed by extraction of a nonempty open from its finite stratification; Stacks Tag 03S0 (etale-cohomology.tex, lemma-etale-stratified-finite).

proof.text: Choose an algebra-isomorphic small model K of E using finite dimensionality over the small field Q_l. Minimal polynomials are preserved by this algebra equivalence, hence so is the spectral absolute value. Postcomposition therefore gives isomorphisms of the continuous rational coefficient sheaves and integral coefficient sheaves, with a commuting scalar square. Transport finite local freeness through these isomorphisms and through the explicit continuous-module encoding.

Apply the existing continuous etale-local lattice theorem, which already collects finitely many affine neighborhoods into a qcqs etale surjection p:Y to X and a locally finite free integral lattice M on Y.

Apply finite-etale stratification to p. The union of the interiors of a finite locally closed stratification is dense (Topology.Stratification.dense_iUnion_interior_stratum), so some interior U is nonempty. Its inclusion into X has image in a selected stratum S. The base change S times_X U to U is a surjective immersion, hence a closed immersion. Since U is reduced, this closed immersion is an isomorphism by Mathlib isIso_of_isClosedImmersion_of_surjective. Its inverse supplies the scheme map U to S. Pullback pasting therefore makes Y times_X U to U finite etale, and surjectivity survives base change.

Pull the lattice M to Y times_X U. Local finite freeness survives inverse image. The scalar-pullback and composition isomorphisms identify its rationalization with the pullback of L restricted to U. The open U has a noetherian underlying space, so finite-etale lattice descent produces a locally finite free integral module on U.

Encode the descended integral module as a sheaf module and transport it back to the original coefficient presentation. The tensor coefficient-square isomorphism commutes with sheafification. The continuous field encoding commutes with etale restriction. For continuous coefficients, composition of site objects is left adjoint to base change; the identity coefficient restriction and pullback-precomposition maps satisfy its unit and counit equations pointwise. The resulting module adjunction and the canonical ringed module adjunction have the same right adjoint, so uniqueness of left adjoints identifies restriction with the exact continuousModulePullback used in the conclusion. Compose these isomorphisms to obtain the required rationalization. Finally U is topologically noetherian, so its inclusion is quasi-compact. No constant or positive rank is required.
